title: Paloma and the Extraction
premise: Ulyana Galloway, a disgraced intelligence analyst living under a borrowed name in a CIA-adjacent safe house, discovers the property has been listed online with interior photos — including her own belongings and a redacted file she thought was destroyed. The listing is bait, set by someone inside the network who wants her flushed out before she can testify about a covert extraction program that disappeared twelve people, including a woman whose identity Ulyana unknowingly assumed. Hunted by an assassin contracted simultaneously by three governments who each want the program buried differently, Ulyana must reconstruct the truth from the photos themselves and reach a dawn extraction flight where a journalist waits. In the end, she chooses not to board: instead she hands the evidence to the assassin — the sister of one of the disappeared — and lets the story detonate without her, finally surrendering the false identity that was never hers.
about_author: Rosalind Quintana is the pen name of a former risk analyst who spent a decade writing threat assessments for organizations she cannot name. She writes thrillers about paper trails, borrowed lives, and the bureaucratic machinery of disappearance.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Scrolling real estate sites out of insomnia-fueled habit, she finds her safe house for sale — every room photographed, including the locked drawer holding her go-bag and a burned file fragment. The emotional beat is cold dread: invisibility, her only currency, has been spent without her consent.

chapters.title: Three Names
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, with an intercut of the handler Marsh. She runs the listing's metadata and finds it uploaded from an agency server she was expelled from three years ago. Marsh denies everything too quickly. Beat: paranoia sharpening into purpose as she realizes someone wants her located — or lured.

chapters.title: What the Camera Saw
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Forensic reading of the photos reveals reflections, timestamps, and a woman's coat in a closet that isn't hers — matching the identity documents she was issued. She begins to suspect her name belonged to someone else first. Beat: vertigo as identity itself becomes unreliable.

chapters.title: The Contractor
chapters.summary: Assassin Ilse Varga's POV. Contracted by three separate governments to retrieve 'the Galloway asset' — each with different termination instructions, meaning whoever gets there first defines the truth. Ilse arrives at the safe house and finds it staged. Beat: professional detachment cracking into curiosity.

chapters.title: Twelve Departures
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Digging through archived flight manifests, she maps the extraction program: twelve people flown out under her assumed name over six years, none arriving. The program didn't move assets; it erased them. Beat: grief and fury braided together.

chapters.title: Safe House Burning
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Ilse corners Ulyana at the house but hesitates when Ulyana shows her a photo — the coat, and a face Ilse recognizes. A third party torches the building; both barely escape. Beat: enemies forced into alliance by a shared enemy's impatience.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sold the Door
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Tracing the listing to a broker, they find the network's quartermaster dead three days — killed after he sold the photos upward, thinking he was negotiating immunity. Beat: the cost of proximity to power made flesh; no one is clean.

chapters.title: Dawn Is a Deadline
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs accelerate. Marsh offers Ulyana reinstatement and a new name if she boards the dawn flight and stays silent; Ilse's three clients converge on the airfield. Ulyana must decide what truth is worth and to whom. Beat: compressed, ticking-clock dread.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV at the airfield. She reaches the plane, sees the journalist waiting, and understands boarding means the story dies with her silence. Ilse arrives with a weapon drawn — and instead hands Ulyana her client list. Beat: climax; betrayal inverted into witness.

chapters.title: Paloma
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, epilogue-adjacent. She gives everything to Ilse — revealed as the sister of the first disappeared woman, Paloma — and walks away from the runway as the flight leaves empty. Weeks later, the program surfaces in three capitals at once. Beat: release; Ulyana finally owns no name but her own.
